text:
mike: FYI: the python sample app we shipped to a couple of customers started looping duplicate pages + 429s when token refresh and our client-side lease-based concurrency are both on. Repro steps below.

sophia: ugh. can you paste logs? is it the SDK or sampleapp logic?

mike: logs: ```
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z ERROR paged-fetcher: token-refresh triggered for user=acct-123
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z INFO leases: releasing 4 leases due to auth_change
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z INFO paginator: last_cursor=eyJpZCI6IjEwMyJ9
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z INFO fetch: request params cursor=eyJpZCI6IjEwMyJ9,page_size=50
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z WARN rate-limit: 429 for request id=abc123
2024-06-13T10:02:12Z INFO paginator: emitting page with cursor=eyJpZCI6IjEwMyJ9
2024-06-13T10:02:13Z ERROR fetcher: duplicate page detected, requeueing
```

mike: tl;dr: token refresh causes leases to be released and workers to restart pagination concurrently. Cursor gets re-used by multiple workers -> duplicate page processing -> downstream emits bursty retries -> platform returns 429s.

ana: (sorry) i mean ana: i saw something similar in node sdk last month but it was auth header swap + in-flight caching TTL.

ana: wanted to check the client config we used:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...,
                      max_leases=8,
                      lease_ttl=2.5,  # seconds
                      page_size=50,
                      retry_policy={"max_retries":3, "on_429_backoff": True},
                      token_refresh_hook=auth_hook)
```

ana: note lease_ttl is very short. token refresh takes ~200-400ms, SDK emits lease release on auth change which makes other workers grab same cursor.

ana: also sampleapp doesnt persist last-seen cursors atomically, so race is possible.

pm-elijah: This looks like a DX-onboarding footgun  1 i mean: default lease_ttl of 2.5s + optimistic lease release on auth change. We should either harden defaults or detect auth-refresh storms and stall leases.

infra-ops: Could we change lease behavior to: on auth change, mark leases as "stalled" for jitter window (e.g., 500-1500ms) instead of immediate release? That would let in-flight pages finish instead of racing.

ana: Agreed. Also add idempotency token per page request and server-side dedupe header if possible: `X-Redwood-Page-Id` based on cursor+session. That prevents duplicate processing if two workers actually fetch same cursor.

sophia: Another mitigation: persist last_cursor to a local lightweight store (sqlite/redis) and use compare-and-swap when claiming next cursor. That required sampleapp change but is safer.

mike: Patch proposal: SDK changes + sampleapp quickfix. SDK: 1) don't release leases instantly on auth swap; set a small stall window with jitter. 2) expose `idempotency_key_for_page(cursor)` helper. 3) document best practices: lease_ttl guidance, token_refresh backoff, and cursor persistence snippet.

mike: Sampleapp quickfix: atomic store for cursor and optional `--disable-lease-release-on-refresh` flag for early customers.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: team=devex, branch=fix/lease-auth-stall, reviewers=@ana,@sophia. CI status pending.

ana: I'll prototype SDK change + tests for race. Will add integration test that simulates token rotations mid-pagination.

pm-elijah: add a short blurb to onboarding docs (sdk best-practices) about auth refresh + leases. That should prevent new users from hitting it.

infra-ops: one more ask: add an observability metric `leases.auth_stalls` and an alert when duplicate-page-for-cursor > 5/min.

mike: OK assigning: ana (SDK patch + tests), sophia (sampleapp atomic cursor), infra-ops (metrics+alert), pm-elijah (docs blurb). I'll open a follow-up thread with links to PRs.

sophia: :thumbsup: will also spin up a small sim harness to validate under high token churn.

mike: thanks all. feel free to @me on PRs.

sophia: minor: can we avoid changing default lease_ttl for existing users? prefer opt-in flag and stronger docs.

ana: yep default stays same, change only in new minor SDK with opt-in env var REDWOOD_LEASE_AUTH_STALL=true by default for next major.

mike: cool. closing this thread after PRs land.

infra-ops: noted  i'll create the alert once PR merges.
